prerequisites: To enroll in this course, it is necessary to have passed or be enrolled in all subjects from courses prior to the one in which this subject is located.

learning_outcomes.text: Understand the dynamic needs of the automobile.
Acquire skills for the design of elements aimed at reducing consumption and emissions.
Know the mechanical design of alternative and low or zero emission propulsion systems.
Ability to develop the different mechanical aspects of the vehicle to optimize its energy efficiency.
Distinguish between PHEV, micro-hybrid, and electric vehicles.
Types of batteries used including inertial batteries.
Proficiency in the use of analysis and simulation tools for multibody systems applied to hybrid vehicle dynamics.
Students must acquire fundamentals of rotordynamics.
Skills in parameterizing variable frequency drives for asynchronous motors.
Principles of structural analysis applied to vehicles.
Knowledge of energy storage systems, charging, and charging stations (electrolineras).

syllabus_topics: Introduction and background. The Gyrobus. Evolution of electric motors and power electronics applied in automotive. Relative inefficiency of combustion engines.
Hybrid and electric vehicle systems and components. Gearboxes. Conventional gearboxes. Applications of epicyclic gear trains to hybrid vehicles.

Hybrid vehicles and the environment. Propulsion system design. Reduction of petroleum consumed in the personal transport sector as an essential factor for achieving energy and environmental sustainability. Classification of electric motor types used in PHEVs. EURO-6 regulations.
Rotordynamics and safety concepts. Study of a Jeffcott rotor. Frequency response. Orbits. Balancing of flexible shafts.
Energy storage systems. Conventional batteries. Inertial batteries.
Dynamic analysis tools and simulation of electric vehicles. Dynamic analysis using multibody system simulation tools.

assessment_methods.method: Practice report, practicum and external practices

assessment_rules: Those who do not follow continuous assessment will take a different exam covering the entire subject than those who do. Ethical commitment: Students are expected to demonstrate appropriate ethical behavior. In case of detecting unethical behavior (copying, plagiarism, unauthorized use of electronic devices, and others), the student is considered not to meet the necessary requirements to pass the course. In this case, the overall grade for the current academic year will be a failure (0.0). The use of any electronic device will not be allowed during evaluation tests unless expressly authorized. Introducing an unauthorized electronic device into the examination room will be considered a reason for not passing the course in the current academic year, and the overall grade will be a failure (0.0).
